CFML Language Reference: Functions

IsAuthenticated

Checks whether the current user has logged in with CFAUTHENTICATE, either in any security context or in the one you name.

Category

Authentication functions

Syntax

IsAuthenticated([ securitycontext ])

Parameters

securitycontext
Optional name of a security context defined on the Advanced Security pages of the Administrator. If omitted, any context will do.

Returns

YES if the user is authenticated, NO otherwise.

Usage

A successful CFAUTHENTICATE sets a CFAUTHORIZATION_context cookie, so the login is remembered on later requests; the stored credentials are checked again each time. When Advanced Security is not set up (no security contexts exist, the way the server ships), nobody is ever authenticated and the function simply returns NO, so pages can test it safely.

Put the check in Application.cfm to protect a whole application, then use IsAuthorized for finer control.

Example

Opens the example in a new window. The example runs on this server, so it only works when you browse from the server itself (127.0.0.1).
<CFIF IsAuthenticated()>
  <CFOUTPUT><P>Welcome back, #AuthenticatedUser()# (context #AuthenticatedContext()#).</CFOUTPUT>
<CFELSE>
  <P>You are not logged in. A real application would show its login form here
  and call CFAUTHENTICATE when it is posted.</P>
</CFIF>
<CFOUTPUT>
<TABLE BORDER=1 CELLPADDING=3>
<TR><TD>IsAuthenticated()</TD><TD>#IsAuthenticated()#</TD></TR>
<TR><TD>IsAuthenticated("Intranet")</TD><TD>#IsAuthenticated("Intranet")#</TD></TR>
</TABLE>
</CFOUTPUT>
